es.summary: Infección bacteriana que afecta cualquier parte del sistema urinario, más frecuente en la vejiga y la uretra. Es la segunda causa de infección en la población y se diagnostica mediante análisis de orina.
key_points: Síntomas típicos: disuria, urgencia, frecuencia y posible fiebre
Diagnóstico: cultivo y examen microscópico de orina
Tratamiento de primera línea: antibióticos según sensibilidad
Prevención: hidratación adecuada e higiene perineal

pathophysiology: Colonización de la uretra por bacterias gram‑negativas (E. coli)
Ascenso ascendente a la vejiga y, en casos graves, a los riñones
Respuesta inflamatoria local produce edema y dolor
Puede progresar a pielonefritis si no se trata
risk_factors: Sexo femenino por anatomía uretral corta
Embarazo, menopausia o uso de anticonceptivos hormonales
Diabetes mellitus y glucosa urinaria elevada
Catéter vesical o cualquier dispositivo urinario
signs_symptoms: Orina turbia, maloliente o con sangre
diagnostics: Análisis de orina: leucocitos ≥10 cél/µL, nitritos positivos
Urocultivo: ≥10⁵ UFC/mL de un solo organismo
Hemograma: leucocitosis si hay respuesta sistémica
Ecografía renal si se sospecha complicación
treatment: Antibiótico de amplio espectro (p. ej. nitrofurantoína, trimetoprim‑sulfametoxazol)
Hidratación oral ≥2 L/día para favorecer el lavado bacteriano
Analgesia con paracetamol o antiinflamatorio si es necesario
En casos complicados, terapia intravenosa y posible hospitalización
nursing_care: Evaluar signos vitales y dolor cada 4 h
Monitorear ingesta y salida de líquidos
Observar cambios en color, olor y aspecto de la orina
Mantener catéter estéril y registrar tiempo de permanencia
Educar sobre higiene perineal y vaciamiento completo
patient_teaching: Beber al menos 2 L de agua al día
Limpiar de adelante hacia atrás al asearse
Completar el ciclo completo de antibióticos
Reportar fiebre o empeoramiento del dolor

related_to: presencia de bacterias en la orina
outcomes: Control de infección: ausencia de fiebre y dolor al orinar en 48 h
Adherencia al tratamiento: completar ciclo antibiótico prescrito

interventions.action: Administrar antibiótico según prescripción y observar reacciones adversas
interventions.rationale: El antibiótico elimina la bacteria causante y previene complicaciones

interventions.action: Monitorear signos de infección (temp, disuria, frecuencia) cada 4 h
interventions.rationale: Detectar rápidamente cualquier empeoramiento o complicación

interventions.action: Fomentar ingesta de líquidos ≥2 L/día
interventions.rationale: Aumenta el flujo urinario y ayuda a eliminar bacterias

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre higiene perineal adecuada
interventions.rationale: Reduce la colonización bacteriana y previene recurrencias

interventions.action: Mantener asepsia del catéter y registrar tiempo de permanencia
interventions.rationale: Disminuye riesgo de infección asociada al dispositivo

outcomes: Capacidad para realizar actividades de la vida diaria sin limitación en 72 h
Dolor reducido a ≤2 en escala de 0‑10

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de dolor y registrar escala cada 4 h
interventions.rationale: Permite ajustar analgesia y medir mejoría

interventions.action: Promover reposo y actividades graduales según tolerancia
interventions.rationale: Evita agotamiento y facilita recuperación

interventions.action: Administrar analgésico según orden médica
interventions.rationale: Alivia el dolor y mejora la capacidad funcional

interventions.action: Fomentar hidratación adecuada (≥2 L/día)
interventions.rationale: Reduce irritación vesical y facilita el vaciamiento

interventions.action: Enseñar técnicas de vaciamiento vesical completo (p. ej. posición sentada con apoyo)
interventions.rationale: Previene retención y disminuye incomodidad

en.summary: Bacterial infection affecting any part of the urinary system, most common in the bladder and urethra. It is the second most common infection in the population and is diagnosed via urine analysis.
key_points: Typical symptoms: dysuria, urgency, frequency, and possible fever
Diagnosis: culture and microscopic urine examination
First-line treatment: antibiotics based on sensitivity
Prevention: adequate hydration and perineal hygiene

pathophysiology: Colonization of the urethra by gram-negative bacteria (E. coli)
Ascending infection to the bladder and, in severe cases, to the kidneys
Local inflammatory response causes edema and pain
Can progress to pyelonephritis if untreated
risk_factors: Female sex due to short urethral anatomy
Pregnancy, menopause, or use of hormonal contraceptives
Diabetes mellitus and elevated urinary glucose
Bladder catheter or any urinary device
Spinal cord injury with urinary retention
diagnostics: Urine culture: ≥10⁵ CFU/mL of a single organism
treatment: Oral hydration ≥2 L/day to promote bacterial flushing
Analgesia with acetaminophen or anti-inflammatory if needed
In complicated cases, intravenous therapy and possible hospitalization
nursing_care: Assess vital signs and pain every 4 h
Observe changes in urine color, odor, and appearance
Maintain sterile catheter and record dwell time
Educate on perineal hygiene and complete voiding
patient_teaching: Drink at least 2 L of water per day
Clean from front to back when wiping

outcomes: Infection control: absence of fever and dysuria within 48 h
Adherence to treatment: complete prescribed antibiotic course

interventions.action: Administer antibiotic per prescription and monitor for adverse reactions
interventions.rationale: The antibiotic eliminates the causative bacteria and prevents complications

interventions.action: Monitor signs of infection (temperature, dysuria, frequency) every 4 h
interventions.rationale: Detect rapid worsening or complications

interventions.action: Encourage fluid intake ≥2 L/day
interventions.rationale: Increases urinary flow and helps eliminate bacteria

interventions.action: Educate patient on proper perineal hygiene
interventions.rationale: Reduces bacterial colonization and prevents recurrences

interventions.action: Maintain catheter asepsis and record dwell time
interventions.rationale: Reduces device-associated infection risk

outcomes: Ability to perform activities of daily living without limitation within 72 h
Pain reduced to ≤2 on a 0‑10 scale

interventions.action: Assess pain level and record scale every 4 h
interventions.rationale: Allows adjustment of analgesia and measurement of improvement

interventions.action: Promote rest and gradual activity as tolerated
interventions.rationale: Prevents exhaustion and facilitates recovery

interventions.action: Administer analgesic per medical order
interventions.rationale: Relieves pain and improves functional capacity

interventions.action: Encourage adequate hydration (≥2 L/day)
interventions.rationale: Reduces bladder irritation and facilitates voiding

interventions.action: Teach techniques for complete bladder emptying (e.g., seated position with support)
interventions.rationale: Prevents retention and decreases discomfort

summary.0.quote: A urinary tract infection (UTI) is a bacterial infection affecting any part of the urinary system; a UTI that affects the kidneys is called pyelonephritis .

key_points.4.quote: Drinking plenty of fluids and maintaining good hygiene can help prevent recurrent UTIs.

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: The urge to urinate multiple times throughout the day or night (nocturia) is urinary frequency . It is often accompanied by a compelling sense of urgency, introducing another layer of concern.

sections.signs_symptoms.2.quote: Urine that smells bad or looks cloudy or reddish

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: Indications for urinary catheterization include urinary retention , surgical procedures, the need to monitor urine output in critically ill patients, the facilitation of healing in certain medical conditions, and to monitor the effectiveness of treatments provided to the patient to measure expected improved p

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: The examination encompasses various aspects, including the physical properties of urine, such as color, clarity, and odor, as well as chemical and microscopic elements such as pH levels, specific gravity, and the presence of proteins, glucose, blood cells, and crystals.
